previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for an acute flare of chronic pancreatitis, presenting with severe epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the back, nausea, and persistent vomiting. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and her standard IV pain and anti-nausea regimen, including Dilaudid, Ketorolac, Phenergan, and Ondansetron. Her pain gradually improved, and she was advanced from NPO to clear liquids, then to a regular diet. She restarted her home oral medications, including methadone, amitriptyline, and lisinopril, with a temporary increase in lisinopril dose for blood pressure control. Due to subtherapeutic INR on admission, she was bridged with daily Lovenox while restarting Coumadin, with discharge instructions to take 10 mg Coumadin on the evening of discharge, then 7.5 mg daily, continuing Lovenox until INR was therapeutic for over 24 hours. Her J-tube and port site remained clean, and she remained ambulatory throughout. She was discharged home with home health support for anticoagulation management and follow-up arranged.

Brief Hospital Course:
# Chronic pancreatitis: Ms ___ presented with her typical 
symptoms associated with her pancreatitis flare, epigastric pain 
radiatin to the back, nausea and vomiting. Pain improved with 
her usual pain regimen detailed below. Admission labs showed a 
___ criteria of 0 with a predicted mortality of 1%. 
Triglycerides 146. No evidence of obstruction. Given lack of 
distension and typical features no imaging was pursued. She was 
started on her typical pancreatitis flare regimen:
Dilaudid 8mg IV Q2hrs (hang  w/ 50cc bag NS and infuse over 
15min), 
Ketorolac 15mg IV Q6hrs 
Ondansetron 4mg IV Q8hrs (hang w/50cc bag NS and infuse over 
15min)
Phenergan 25 mg IV Q4hrs (hang w/ 50cc bag NS and infuse over 
15min)
Lorazepam 0.5mg IV Q4hrs Lorazepam 1 mg qhs. 
continuous IVF D5W/ ___ at 125ml/hr 

She was keep NPO and slowly the diet was advanced. On discharge 
she was tolerating her regular diet, tube feeds and home PO pain 
medications.

# Fevers/GNR: Pt spiked a fever for two days and when Cx'ed, had 
GNRs grow out of blood Cxs x 3.  Was started on Zosyn IV.  ID 
was c/s'ed, and felt that could treat through the port with abx 
dwells.  After speaking with both PEVA RNs and pharmacy, 
determined only ceftaz would be stable enough to be used as a 
port lock.  That was started as Q12h lock alternating port sites 
Q12H to be continued with ___ at home for a total of a ___fter 3 days of Zosyn, Cx notably had changed 
sensitivities, so changed to Ceftazidime IV.  Of note, BLood Cxs 
became negative after switching to Ceftazidime therapy.  She was 
discharged with ___ services to continue ceftaz abx as well as 
ceftaz dwells for a total ___s per ID, no need for 
safety labs, and they recommend blood cx repeated 1 week after 
cessation of abx (pt will have these cultures drawn at the time 
of her f/u appt with her PCP).  Teaching was done in house to 
ensure the pt knew how to do abx dwells and abx therapy at home.

# Left upper ext DVT on coumadin: Admitted while on coumadin 
(last DVT ___ but given difficulty with PO intake she was 
transitioned to SQ lovenox when the INR was < 2.0. Once taking 
POs she was restarted on coumadin with a lovenox bridge. Given 
her h/o of multiple DVTs and current port we believe she 
warrents ongoing coumadin therapy after the traditional 3 month 
treatment. She required dosages as high as 15 mg to reach 
therapeutic levels. At discharge, her INR was 2.3 -> she was 
instructed to take 10 mg of coumadin until ___, when 
her INR is checked and she can have her dose changed (was on 7.5 
daily prior to admission, and had INR of 3.3 at time of 
admission).  Information was sent to her ___ clinic for 
continuity of care.

# HTN: Blood pressure as high as the 150s/100s. Likely 
exacerbated ___ to her pain. Held lisinopril given NPO/ vomiting 
initially and treated with prn IV hydral. Once taking POs 
lisinipril was restarted and increased to 40mg daily. As her 
pain declined, her blood pressure trended down and she was 
discharged on her home dose of lisinopril 10 mg. 

# Anemia: Pt has h/o Fe-deficiency anemia, and Hct noted to 
trend down inhouse in the setting of IVF (likely dilutional).  
Even so, iron indices and retic count were checked which 
indicated Fe deficiency anemia.  We treated the patient with IV 
iron in an effort to augment erythropoiesis.  The pt felt that 
the IV iron assisted her in eventual recovery given her recent 
si/sxs of fatigue and feeling ""rundown.""  Hct started to recover 
after IV Iron.  Further IV iron was deferred given possible 
bacteremia.

# Depression: Pt was maintained on lorazepam in house for her 
anxiety/depression, and was d/c'ed back on her home regimen 
which includes amitryptiline.
